defects: Adds hypothesis that R is a Ring and an IsDomain, whereas gold only requires R to be a Semiring with Nontrivial R — this restricts the theorem to domains and drops the intended generality (e.g. rings with zero divisors are excluded).

Formalizes torsion via 'r ≠ 0 ∧ r • m = 0' instead of the non-zero-divisor condition (r ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) used in Module.IsTorsion; these coincide only when R is a domain, so under the produced statement's added IsDomain hypothesis they happen to agree, but this makes the produced theorem a strictly weaker special case rather than the same proposition as the gold's IsTorsion-based statement.
Overall the produced theorem is a corollary of the gold theorem (holds under strictly stronger hypotheses on R), not an equivalent restatement of the same proposition.
